problems.problem_orig:
O veículo de sondagem VS-30 é desenvolvido pelo Instituto de Aeronáutica e Espaço (IAE) para realizar experimentos em ambiente de microgravidade. Não possuindo energia suficiente para atingir a velocidade orbital, tais foguetes descrevem uma trajetória aproximadamente parabólica e retornam à superfície terrestre, conforme ilustrado na Figura abaixo. O VS-30 possui um único motor-foguete, denominado S30. Este motor funciona por 30 segundos, levando o foguete a 25 km de altitude. Findo o combustível, o S30 é descartado e cai. Conforme mostrado na Figura abaixo, o que restou do foguete, a carga útil, continua, por inércia, o seu vôo ascendente, mas, em função da ação da gravidade e do atrito com a atmosfera terrestre (até 100 km de altitude), sua velocidade é reduzida até alcançar a altitude máxima (apogeu). A partir do apogeu a carga útil, atraída pela gravidade terrestre, inicia o seu movimento de retorno à superfície terrestre. Para atenuar a velocidade de impacto com a superfície terrestre, a carga-útil é dotada de um sistema de paraquedas. Caso contrário, o impacto com o solo danificaria os experimentos levados ao espaço.

Pergunta 6a) (0,25 pontos) A partir da Figura acima qual é o apogeu da carga útil do VS-30?

Pergunta 6b) (0,25 pontos) A distância entre o ponto de lançamento do foguete e o ponto de impacto da carga útil é denominada alcance. A partir da Figura acima qual é o alcance do VS-30?

Pergunta 6c) (0,5 ponto) Acima dos 100 km de altitude, são estabelecidas as condições de microgravidade, ou seja, qualquer objeto solto no interior da carga útil do foguete flutuará, tal qual os astronautas flutuam no interior das suas espaçonaves. A partir da Figura acima qual é o tempo de microgravidade (em segundos) proporcionado pelo vôo do VS-30?

problems.problem:
Remote sensing satellites carry on board sensors that capture images of the Earth's surface. One of the characteristics of the sensors is the spatial resolution, which is their ability to identify objects according to their size. A sensor with a spatial resolution of 1 metre, for example, is able to detect objects such as trees, houses, etc. Images obtained by a sensor with a spatial resolution above 250 m can be used to study continental and oceanic areas and phenomena of large proportions, for example, sea currents and the displacement of air masses. Thus, depending on the spatial resolution, and on other characteristics of the sensors, satellite images are used in the study of different objects, areas, phenomena and environments of the Earth's surface.

Question 8) (0.3 point for each correct answer) (0.1 bonus if you get all 3 right) Based on this information, associate the images with different types of spatial resolution (left column) with the most suitable application (right column).

Left column:
(1) Images with a spatial resolution of 1 m
(2) Images with a spatial resolution of 30 m
(3) Images with a spatial resolution of 1000 m

Right column (each item with an empty pair of parentheses to be filled in):
( ) Map deforested areas (considering a minimum mapped area of 900 m$^2$, that is, 30 x 30 m)
( ) Identify aircraft on an airport runway
( ) Follow the displacement of cold fronts
problems.problem_orig:

Uma das características dos sensores é a resolução espacial, a qual é sua capacidade de identificar objetos em função do tamanho destes. Um sensor com resolução espacial de 1 metro, por exemplo, é capaz de detectar objetos como árvores, casas, etc. Imagens obtidas por um sensor com resolução espacial acima de 250 m, podem ser utilizadas para estudar áreas e fenômenos continentais e oceânicos de grande proporção, por exemplo, correntes marítimas e o deslocamento de massas de ar. Desse modo, dependendo da resolução espacial, e de outras características dos sensores, as imagens de satélite são utilizadas no estudo de diferentes objetos, áreas, fenômenos e ambientes da superfície terrestre.

problems.problem:
In 2009 we celebrated the International Year of Astronomy and in 2011 the International Year of Chemistry, but we also celebrate the 50 years of the first flight into space by the Russian astronaut Yuri Gagarin on 12 April 1961. He made one revolution around the Earth in 108 minutes and said a very famous phrase: "The Earth is blue".

On 20 July 1969 two North American astronauts walked for the first time on the Moon and the first to step on the lunar soil, Neil Armstrong, also said another phrase that became famous: "That's one small step for a man, but a giant leap for mankind".

Question 1a) (0.5 point) Why do you think Yuri Gagarin said that the Earth is blue? Put an X on the correct alternative.

a) Everybody knows that on the Earth there is more water than land and that water is blue, so the Earth is blue.
b) Everybody knows that air is blue, so, seen from space, the Earth is blue.
c) The glass of the little window of the Vostok 1 spacecraft, where Gagarin was, was blue, so he said that the Earth was blue.
d) The white light that comes from the Sun is the mixture of the colours we see in the rainbow, so blue is among them. The blue colour is the most scattered by the atmosphere, to all sides, so from the Earth we see the sky blue and from space it seems that the whole Earth is blue.

Question 1b) (0.25 point for each correct answer) How many years and months after Yuri Gagarin made the first flight into space did Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walk on the Moon? (Answer in years and in months.)
problems.problem_orig:
Em 2009 comemoramos o Ano Internacional da Astronomia e em 2011 o Ano Internacional da Química, mas também comemoramos os 50 anos do primeiro voo ao espaço pelo astronauta russo Yuri Gagarin em 12 de abril de 1961. Ele deu uma volta ao redor da Terra em 108 minutos e disse uma frase muito famosa: "A Terra é azul".

Em 20 de julho de 1969 dois astronautas norte-americanos caminharam pela primeira vez sobre a Lua e o primeiro a pisar o solo lunar, Neil Armstrong, também disse outra frase que ficou famosa: "Este é um pequeno passo para um homem, mas é um salto gigantesco para a humanidade".

Pergunta 1a) (0,5 ponto) Por que será que Yuri Gagarin disse que a Terra é a azul? Coloque um X na alternativa correta.

Read the questions below before reading the statement. This can help. We will consider a rocket of mass 17300 kg placing a satellite of 100 kg in Earth orbit, as illustrated in the figure beside. After the countdown the combustion of the 10000 kg of propellant (fuel + oxidiser) of the 1st stage begins, making the rocket reach a velocity of 1650 m/s. The empty tank of the 1st stage is then discarded, falling into the sea. Soon after the motor of the 2nd stage is started, consuming a further 3000 kg of propellant and increasing the velocity of the part that remained of the rocket (3rd stage and satellite) by 1950 m/s, relative to the 1650 m/s already added by the 1st stage. Before starting the ignition of the motor of the 3rd stage it is necessary to discard the empty tank of the 2nd stage and the fairing that protects the satellite from the friction with the Earth's atmosphere. Both fall into the sea. The 3rd stage contains 1000 kg of propellant, but is able to increase the velocity of the rocket by 4122 m/s. As the propellant is consumed, manoeuvres are carried out with the aim of making the satellite be positioned tangentially to the Earth's surface, as illustrated in the figure. Finally, the 3rd stage is separated from the satellite, both remaining in Earth orbit. problems.problem:
Leap Year. Our calendar is based on the Tropical Year. This is the time that the Sun, in its apparent annual motion, takes between being overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn, going and being overhead at the Tropic of Cancer and returning to be overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn. When the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn or of Cancer, we say that the Summer Solstice is occurring there. To go from one Tropic to the other, it passes overhead at the Celestial Equator and when this occurs we say that the Equinox is occurring. That is why we call it the Tropical Year, since the Sun oscillates between the two Tropics. The duration of this Tropical Year is approximately 365.25 days. Its great advantage is that the seasons of the year always begin, approximately, on the same dates, besides being simple to observe the Equinoxes and the Solstices.

Below we show a schematic figure illustrating this oscillation of the Sun in its apparent annual motion between the tropics, assuming the Earth to be motionless, of course.

Schematic figure of the oscillation of the Sun between the two tropics. In this figure HN and HS mean Northern and Southern Hemisphere, respectively. This "oscillation" of the Sun only occurs because of the tilt of the Earth's rotation axis relative to the perpendicular to the plane of its orbit. If the rotation axis were perpendicular to the plane of the orbit none of this would happen and there would be no seasons of the year.

Question 4a) (0.5 point) In our calendar the year has 365 days, so how many hours are left over each year? Warning: The answer must be in hours.

Question 4b) (0.5 point) When the leftovers add up to one day, after 4 years, we add a day in February and call this year "leap". This year has 366 days. 2012 is a leap year, as were 2008 and will be 2016. The question is: Will 2056 be a leap year?

problems.problem_orig:
Ano Bissexto. Nosso calendário está baseado no Ano Trópico. Este é o tempo que o Sol, em seu movimento aparente anual, gasta entre ficar a pino no Trópico de Capricórnio, ir e ficar a pino ao Trópico de Câncer e voltar a ficar a pino no Trópico de Capricórnio. Quando o Sol está a pino no Trópico de Capricórnio ou de Câncer, dizemos que ali está ocorrendo o Solstício de Verão. Para ir de um Trópico para o outro, passa a pino pelo Equador Celeste e quando isso ocorre dizemos que está ocorrendo o Equinócio. É por isso que o chamamos de Ano Trópico, pois o Sol oscila entre os dois Trópicos. A duração deste Ano Trópico é de, aproximadamente, 365,25 dias. Sua grande vantagem é que as estações do ano sempre começam, aproximadamente, nas mesmas datas, além de ser simples a observação dos Equinócios e dos Solstícios.

Abaixo mostramos uma figura esquemática ilustrando esta oscilação do Sol em seu aparente movimento anual entre os trópicos, supondo a Terra imóvel, claro.

Figura esquemática da oscilação do Sol entre os dois trópicos. Nesta figura HN e HS significam Hemisfério Norte e Sul, respectivamente. Esta "oscilação" do Sol só ocorre devido à inclinação do eixo de rotação da Terra em relação à perpendicular ao plano de sua órbita. Se o eixo de rotação fosse perpendicular ao plano da órbita nada disso aconteceria e não haveria estações do ano.

Pergunta 4a) (0,5 ponto) Em nosso calendário o ano tem 365 dias, então, quantas horas sobram em cada ano? Atenção: A resposta precisa ser em horas.

problems.problem:
In 2011 a total of 95 artificial satellites were placed in Earth orbit. Rockets are the vehicles used to carry the satellites to space. Most of the 57 rockets launched in 2011 carried a single satellite, but there was the case of a rocket that took seven satellites to space at once. The masses of the satellites launched in the year 2011 varied between 3 kg and 18000 kg. But why so many satellites? Satellites are used, for example, for live television broadcasts, allowing an event that takes place in Brazil (the World Cup, for example) to be watched all over the globe almost instantaneously. Satellites are also used to monitor deforestation in the Amazon region, as well as for the transmission of banking data. The signal of the global positioning system, known by the acronym GPS, whose receivers today equip cars, mobile phones and portable computers, also comes from space. Based on the information given, answer the following questions:

Question 7a) (0.25 point) Considering that a year is made up of 52 weeks, how many rockets were launched, on average, per week in the year 2011?

Question 7b) (0.25 point) How many satellites, on average, were launched per week in the year 2011?

Question 7c) (0.5 point) Of the 95 satellites taken to space in 2011, 42 were communications satellites. What percentage of communications satellites were launched in the year 2011?

Since the Soviet Union placed the satellite Sputnik in orbit, in 1957, almost six thousand satellites have been launched into space. On average two satellites are placed in orbit per week. Among the applications of these satellites, it is worth highlighting: Communications, Meteorology, Earth Observation, Data Transmission and the Global Positioning System, known in the western world by the acronym GPS. The dashed lines shown in the figure illustrate the orbits of satellites around the Earth. Polar orbits are those that pass through the North and South poles of the Earth. Earth Observation satellites make use of polar orbits about 800 km from the Earth's surface. Equatorial orbits are typical of Communications satellites, which are at approximately 35800 km from the Earth's surface. As the name suggests, these orbits are in the plane of the Earth's equator. problems.problem:
In Astronomy we often need to measure the angular separation of two bodies or the angular size of a body. Suppose that in the figure below, $L$ is the diameter of the Moon, that is, 3476 km and $R$ its mean distance to the Earth, which is 384000 km. With this the angular diameter subtended by the Moon, seen from the Earth, is:

$$\theta = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{3476\ \text{km}}{384000\ \text{km}} = 0.009\ \text{radians}.$$

But 1 radian is about 60 degrees, so the angular diameter of the Moon, seen from the Earth, is, in degrees, $\theta = 0.009 \times 60\ \text{degrees} = 0.54\ \text{degrees}$.

problems.problem_orig:
Na Astronomia frequentemente precisamos medir a separação angular de dois astros ou o tamanho angular de um astro. Suponha que na figura abaixo, $L$ seja o diâmetro da Lua, isto é, 3.476 km e $R$ sua distância média à Terra, que é de 384.000 km. Com isso o diâmetro angular compreendido pela Lua, vista da Terra, é de:

$$\theta = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{3.476\ \text{km}}{384.000\ \text{km}} = 0{,}009\ \text{radianos}.$$

Mas, 1 radiano é cerca de 60 graus, logo o diâmetro angular da Lua, vista da Terra é, em graus, de $\theta = 0{,}009 \times 60\ \text{graus} = 0{,}54\ \text{graus}$.

Pergunta 6a) (0,4 ponto) Recentemente o astrônomo Dr. Marcelo Emílio, da Universidade de Ponta Grossa, PR, e outros colegas, mediram, com grande precisão, o diâmetro do Sol. problems.problem:
(0.25 point for each correct answer) You learned to find the cardinal directions according to the method contained in many textbooks, which says "open your right arm towards where the Sun rises and there is the East direction, to your left will be the West, in front of you the North and behind you the South." Well, this process is not at all precise, since the Sun can even rise and set in the South, or even not rise anywhere depending on the place and season where you are. These "strange" situations occur for latitudes between the poles and the polar circles. But let us see how Juliana and her mother, Mrs Vilma, did to determine correctly the cardinal directions in the yard of their house. You can do the same, of course!

First, in the morning, Mrs Wilma stood in the yard and Juliana drew her shadow on the ground, going from between her mother's feet to the top of the shadow of her head (Fig. A). Then Juliana drew a circle on the ground, with a radius equal to that of her mother's shadow (Fig. B). Then Juliana left Mrs Wilma standing in the same place (mothers suffer....) until in the afternoon her shadow reached the drawn circle again, because in this way, of course, the two shadows would be of the same length. Mrs Wilma, to make sure that Juliana was doing everything right, at this moment turned to the side where her shadow was (Fig. C).

Question 7) (0.25 point for each correct answer) To determine the cardinal directions Juliana drew the bisector of the two shadows of her mother (dashed line) and the perpendicular to it (dotted line) (Fig. D). Write the cardinal directions (North, South, East, West) inside the white boxes (Fig. D) at the ends of the dashed and dotted lines.

The Institute of Aeronautics and Space (IAE) is the most important organisation that designs and develops rockets in Brazil. The figure shows the typical flight of a rocket, made up of the rocket motor and the payload. The rocket motor carries the propellant (= fuel + oxidiser) that drives the payload towards space. When the propellant is finished the structure of the rocket motor is separated from the payload, falling into the sea. The payload (where the experiments are carried) continues its ascending motion, until reaching the maximum height, called apogee. While it flies above 100 km, microgravity conditions are created. In these conditions, any loose object inside it floats. After the apogee the payload returns to the Earth's surface. To reduce the impact velocity with the water, the recovery system (parachute) is activated. After falling into the sea the payload is rescued by a helicopter. See the schematic illustration above.

(0.2 point for each correct answer) Artificial satellites are made by humans to revolve around the Earth with the most diverse objectives. The path travelled by satellites around the Earth is called an orbit. The orbits of most satellites resemble a circle. Rockets are used to place satellites in orbit. The distance of satellites from the Earth's surface varies according to the desired application. For example, if the objective of the satellite is to obtain images of the Earth's surface it is positioned in an orbit whose distance from the Earth's surface can vary between 700 km and 900 km. This type of satellite has a velocity of 27000 km/h. Communications satellites are placed at 36000 km from the Earth's surface at a velocity of 11000 km/h. The Moon is the natural satellite of the Earth. It revolves around it at a mean distance of 384000 km and with a velocity of 3600 km/h.

Of the roughly 1200 satellites currently in operation in orbit around the Earth, 400 are for communications. They travel in circular orbits located in the plane of the Equator. The distance of these satellites from the Earth's surface is such that they revolve around the Earth with the same rotation period as the Earth. Satellites are used to monitor flooded areas in the Pantanal Mato-grossense region. The figures beside represent, schematically, two images obtained from the Terra/MODIS satellite. One of them was obtained in a rainy year (2000) while the other in a year with little rain (2009). The images obtained by satellite sensors capture the energy of the Sun that is reflected by the Earth's surface. The sensors work like the eyes of the satellite. Thus, the greater the amount of energy reflected by the Earth's surface, the greater the amount of energy that is captured by the sensors. In practice the images are formed by a set of points ("pixels"), each of which is assigned a "colour", which varies from white to black, with various shades of grey between them. The closer to black, the smaller the amount of energy detected by the sensors.

As imagens obtidas pelos sensores de satélites captam a energia do Sol que é refletida pela superfície terrestre. Os sensores funcionam como os olhos do satélite. Na prática as imagens são formadas por um conjunto de pontos ("pixels"), sendo a cada um deles atribuído uma "cor", que varia do branco ao preto, com vários tons de cinza entre eles. problems.problem:
For rockets to carry people or satellites (of up to 5000 kg) to space (the region beyond the atmosphere), they need to cross the atmosphere (layer of 100 km), which offers a lot of friction, and also need to reach the velocity of 27000 km/h. For this they use 450000 kg of propellant (fuel plus oxidiser). At launch they have 500000 kg of initial total mass (= propellant + satellite + structures) and approximate height of a 20-storey building. In order not to carry useless "weight" to space the rocket is made in two stages (= two tanks with an engine in each tank). When the first tank runs out, it and its engine are ejected and fall into the sea, as the figure beside illustrates. When the atmosphere ends, the fairing is also ejected so that the rocket becomes even "lighter". The second stage, finally, manages to reach the velocity of 27000 km/h and then ejects the satellite, which enters orbit. The second stage also stays in orbit and is called space junk.

( ) The empty tank of the second stage engine becomes space junk.
( ) The mass of the satellite represents 10% of the total initial mass of the rocket.
( ) The rocket has stages in order to reach space "light".

problems.problem_orig:
Para que os foguetes levem pessoas ou satélites (de até 5.000 kg) ao espaço (região além da atmosfera), precisam atravessar a atmosfera (camada de 100 km), a qual oferece muito atrito, e ainda precisam atingir a velocidade de 27.000 km/h. Para tanto usam 450.000 kg de propelente (combustível mais oxidante). No lançamento têm 500.000 kg de massa total inicial (= propelente + satélite + estruturas) e altura aproximada de um prédio de 20 andares. Para não levar "peso" inútil ao espaço o foguete é feito em dois estágios (= dois tanques com um motor em cada tanque). Quando acaba o primeiro tanque, ele e seu motor são ejetados e caem no mar, conforme ilustra a figura ao lado. Quando termina a atmosfera, também a coifa é ejetada para o foguete ficar ainda mais "leve". O segundo estágio, finalmente, consegue atingir a velocidade de 27.000 km/h e então ejeta o satélite, que entra em órbita. O segundo estágio também fica em órbita e é chamado de lixo espacial.

7a) (0.5 point) What size will the Sun be seen, in degrees, by the astronauts on Mars? Let us help with an example. Suppose that, in the figure beside, $L$ is the diameter of the Moon, that is, 3476 km and $R$ its mean distance to the Earth, which is 384000 km. Then the angular diameter ($\theta$) subtended by the Moon, seen from the Earth, is:

$$\theta = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{3476\ \text{km}}{384000\ \text{km}} = 0.009\ \text{radians}.$$

But 1 radian is about 60 degrees. So the angular diameter of the Moon seen from the Earth is, in degrees, $\theta = 0.009 \times 60\ \text{degrees} = 0.54\ \text{degrees}$. Coincidentally, this is practically the same angular diameter of the Sun seen from the Earth.

Repeat the calculation above and calculate the angular diameter of the Sun, in degrees, seen from Mars. Data: diameter of the Sun, about 1400000 km, and mean distance to Mars, about 228000000 km.

problems.problem:
As you already know from question 1, the luminosity of a star depends on its radius and its surface temperature. Through the equation below, we can find out how many times the radius of a star is larger (or smaller) than the radius of the Sun if we know how much more (or less) luminous than the Sun it is and how much hotter (or colder) than the Sun it is:

$$\text{star radius} = \frac{\sqrt{\text{star luminosity}}}{(\text{star temperature})^2} \rightarrow R = \frac{\sqrt{L}}{T^2}$$

Let us give an example: if a star is 4 times more luminous than the Sun and has twice its surface temperature, then its radius will be:

$$\text{radius} = \frac{\sqrt{4}}{(2)^2} = \frac{2}{4} = 0.5 \ \text{(the star has a radius 0.5 times the radius of the Sun)}$$

problems.problem_orig:
Como você já sabe da questão 1, a luminosidade de uma estrela depende do seu raio e da sua temperatura superficial. Através da equação abaixo, podemos descobrir quantas vezes o raio das estrelas é maior (ou menor) do que o raio do Sol se soubermos o quanto ela é mais (ou menos) luminosa do que o Sol e o quanto ela é mais (ou menos) quente do que o Sol:

$$\text{raio da estrela} = \frac{\sqrt{\text{luminosidade da estrela}}}{(\text{temperatura da estrela})^2} \rightarrow R = \frac{\sqrt{L}}{T^2}$$

Vamos dar um exemplo: se uma estrela é 4 vezes mais luminosa do que o Sol e tem o dobro da sua temperatura superficial, então seu raio será:

$$\text{raio} = \frac{\sqrt{4}}{(2)^2} = \frac{2}{4} = 0{,}5 \ \text{(a estrela tem um raio 0,5 vezes o raio do Sol)}$$

(0.2 for each correct answer) Kepler's three Laws (1571 – 1630) describe the motions of planets, moons, comets, artificial satellites etc. and for the planets they say the following:

1st Law: "The orbit of each planet is an ellipse, with the Sun at one of the foci."
2nd Law: "A straight line between the Sun and the planet "sweeps" equal areas in equal intervals of time." Hence the speed of the planet is variable, being maximum near the Sun and minimum far from the Sun.
3rd Law: "The square of the Period ($P$) divided by the cube of the mean distance ($D$) of the planet to the Sun is a constant ($k$)." That is, $P^2/D^3 = k$.

b) B / C - At which of the points, B or C, is the speed of the Earth minimum?
c) ANOTHER STAR / NOTHING - If the Sun is at $F_1$, then what exists at $F_2$?
d) BLACK HOLE / NOTHING - What exists exactly at the geometric centre of the ellipse?
e) A / B - Is the speed of the Earth increasing when it approaches A or B?

(0.2 for each correct answer) The time (period) for the Earth to go once around the Sun, measured relative to the stars, lasts 365.2564 days and is called the sidereal year. But, in fact, we use the tropical year, to keep the beginning of the seasons constant. The tropical year lasts approximately 365.25 days, but on the calendar we only have 365 days. Therefore, every year there is "left over" 1/4 (one quarter = 0.25) of a day, so every 4 years a day is added and this year is called a leap year.

Kepler's First Law, also called the Law of Orbits, describes the motions of planets, moons, comets and artificial satellites around the bodies they orbit.

Kepler's First Law for the planets says the following:
"The orbit of each planet is an ellipse, with the Sun at one of the foci."

Kepler's First Law for the satellites of Jupiter says the following:
"The orbit of each moon of Jupiter is an ellipse, with Jupiter at one of the foci."

Kepler's First Law for the satellites of Saturn says the following:
"The orbit of each moon of Saturn is an ellipse, with Saturn at one of the foci."

Mark the correct statement of Kepler's First Law for the Earth and its artificial satellites.
a) The orbit of each artificial satellite of the Earth is an ellipse, with the Earth at one of the foci.
b) The orbit of each moon of Saturn is an ellipse, with Saturn at one of the foci.
c) The orbit of each moon of Jupiter is an ellipse, with Jupiter at one of the foci.
d) The orbit of each planet is an ellipse, with the Sun at one of the foci.
e) Artificial satellites do not obey Kepler's First Law.

The Brazilian satellite Amazonia 1, launched on 28/02/21, is about 750 km above the Earth's surface. The company Visiona Tecnologia Espacial S.A., located in São José dos Campos, SP, is developing the nanosatellite VCUB1, of 10 kg mass, which will be in a polar orbit of 710 km, as the figure shows. Reminder: speed = distance/time.

From the information above put F (false) or T (true) in the statements below.
a) Neptune is the planet with the smallest translation speed.
b) The orbital speed of the VCUB1 is greater than that of the Brazilian satellite Amazonia 1.
c) The orbital period of Mercury is the smallest of all the planets.
d) The orbit of the VCUB1 is polar, therefore it does not obey Kepler's Third Law.
e) The orbital period of the VCUB1 is greater than that of the Brazilian satellite Amazonia 1.

problems.problem:
The brightness of a star depends on its distance from us, just like a lamp (for example, of 60 W), which, when near us, shines more than when far. However, the power of the lamp (60 W) does not change whether it is near us or not.

In the constellation of Orion (see the image) we have the stars of the "three Marys", which are in fact Alnitak, Alnilam and Mintaka.

However, Mintaka shines less than Alnitak, although its power (in astronomy we call it Luminosity) is almost twice that of Alnitak.

Mark the correct explanation for this.
a) Mintaka shines less, although it is more luminous, because it is farther away than Alnitak.
b) Mintaka shines less because there is a lot of interstellar dust between it and the Earth.
c) Mintaka shines less because its surface colour is more opaque.
d) Mintaka shines less because it must be much smaller than Alnitak.
e) Mintaka shines less because it is inside the Great Orion Nebula.

[The photograph is not reproduced here (its author is not credited in the paper). It is on page 2 of the official paper: https://sistema.oba.org.br/sisglob/sisglob_arquivos/downloads/Prova%20n%C3%ADvel%203%20da%2025%20OBA%20de%202022.pdf]

b) Mintaka brilha menos porque há muita poeira interestelar entre ela e a Terra.
c) Mintaka brilha menos porque sua cor superficial é mais opaca.
d) Mintaka brilha menos porque deve ser muito menor do que Alnitak.
e) Mintaka brilha menos porque está dentro da Grande Nuvem de Órion.

problems.problem:
The speed of light, and of any electromagnetic radiation, in vacuum, is a constant that is approximately 300000 km/s. The speed of light does not depend on the speed of the emitting source or on the speed of whoever receives the light. The star Betelgeuse is approximately 720 light-years from the Earth and the star Antares is approximately 605 light-years from the Earth. Both are red supergiants with diameters approximately 900 times larger than that of the Sun. Note: a light-year is the distance that light travels in a period of one year.

FIRST write F (false) or T (true) in front of each statement and THEN choose the option that contains the correct sequence of F and T.

1st) The light that we receive today from Betelgeuse is older than the light that we receive today from Antares.
2nd) If Betelgeuse is moving away from the Earth and Antares is approaching the Earth, the speed of the light that they emit in our direction is the same.
3rd) The Betelgeuse that we see today is in fact as it was 720 years ago.
4th) It is impossible to see Antares or Betelgeuse exactly as they are today.
5th) The speed of light is 300000 km/s because the stars are red.

Mark the option that contains the correct sequence of F and T.
a) 1st (T) - 2nd (T) - 3rd (T) - 4th (T) - 5th (F)
b) 1st (T) - 2nd (T) - 3rd (F) - 4th (T) - 5th (F)
c) 1st (F) - 2nd (F) - 3rd (T) - 4th (T) - 5th (F)
d) 1st (T) - 2nd (T) - 3rd (F) - 4th (F) - 5th (T)

$$L = 4\pi\sigma R^2 T^4,$$

where $\sigma$ (Greek letter sigma) is a constant, like $\pi$ (pi), $R$ is the radius of the star and $T$ is the surface temperature of the star. For two stars to have the same Luminosity, they need to have:

Mark the only correct option.

b) They need to have the same radius and the same distance to the Earth.
c) They need to have the same surface Temperature.
d) They need to have the same surface Temperature and the same distance to the Earth.
e) They need to have the same product $RT$.
problems.problem_orig:

$$L = 4\pi\sigma R^2 T^4,$$

onde $\sigma$ (letra grega sigma) é uma constante, como o $\pi$ (pi), $R$ é o raio da estrela e $T$ a temperatura superficial da estrela. Para que duas estrelas tenham a mesma Luminosidade, elas precisam ter:

Assinale a única alternativa correta.

problems.problem:
You have probably noticed that stars have different brightnesses, but you have also noticed that the lamp near your house shines more brightly than another, identical one (of the same Power, for example, 100 Watts), that is 10 blocks away from you. Therefore, the brightness depends on the distance from the light source to the observer.

Astronomers call the Power of stars Luminosity ($L$) and have found that it depends on the Radius ($R$) and the surface Temperature ($T$) of the star, as follows:

$$L = 4\pi\sigma R^2 T^4,$$

where $\sigma$ (Greek letter sigma) is a constant, like $\pi$ (pi).

The stars Betelgeuse, in the constellation of Orion, and Achernar, in the constellation of Eridanus, have exactly the same brightness. Suppose that they also have the same Luminosity. If they have the same brightness and luminosity, we can state that:

Mark the only correct option.
a) They have the same surface Temperature.
b) They have the same Radius and distance to the Earth.
c) They are at the same distance from the Earth.
d) They have the same surface Temperature and distance to the Earth.
e) Nothing can be stated about their distances to the Earth.

Logo, o brilho depende da distância da fonte da luz até o observador.

Os astrônomos chamam a Potência das estrelas de Luminosidade ($L$) e descobriram que ela depende do Raio ($R$) e da Temperatura superficial ($T$) da estrela, da seguinte forma:

$$L = 4\pi\sigma R^2 T^4,$$

onde $\sigma$ (letra grega sigma) é uma constante, como o $\pi$ (pi).

As estrelas Betelgeuse, da constelação de Órion e Achernar, da constelação de Eridano, têm exatamente o mesmo brilho. Suponha que elas também tenham a mesma Luminosidade. Se elas têm o mesmo brilho e luminosidade, podemos afirmar que:

a) Elas têm a mesma Temperatura superficial.
b) Elas têm o mesmo Raio e distância à Terra.
c) Elas estão à mesma distância da Terra.
d) Elas têm a mesma Temperatura superficial e distância à Terra.
e) Nada é possível afirmar sobre as distâncias delas à Terra.

problems.problem:
We know that the Luminosity ($L$) of stars (equivalent to the Power of light bulbs) is given by:

$$L = (4\pi R^2)\,\sigma T^4,$$

where $\sigma$ (Greek letter sigma) is a constant, like $\pi$ (pi), $R$ is the radius of the star and $T$ is the surface temperature of the star. Note that $4\pi R^2$ represents the surface area of the star. Then, if two stars have the same surface temperature, the one with the greater luminosity will be:

Mark the only correct option.
a) The closer to the Earth.
b) The one with more mass.
c) The one with the greater density.
d) The larger of them.
e) The brighter.

onde $\sigma$ (letra grega sigma) é uma constante, como o $\pi$ (pi), $R$ é o raio da estrela e $T$ a temperatura superficial da estrela. Note que $4\pi R^2$ representa a área superficial da estrela. Então se duas estrelas têm a mesma temperatura superficial, a de maior luminosidade será:

Assinale a única alternativa correta.
a) A mais próxima da Terra.
b) A que tiver mais massa.

problems.problem:

$$L = 4\pi\sigma R^2 T^4,$$

where $\sigma$ (Greek letter sigma) is a constant, like $\pi$ (pi). On the other hand, the brightness of the star depends on how much light reaches our eyes or instruments, therefore the brightness depends on the distance, $d$, at which we are from it. The light of the star spreads out through space as it moves away from the star. With what we explained above, we can state that for one and the same star:

Mark the only correct option.
a) The Luminosity and the brightness of the star do not depend on its distance to the Earth.
b) The Luminosity will be greater the closer the star is to us.
c) The brightness of a star depends only on its luminosity.
d) The higher the temperature of the star, the greater its brightness.
e) Its brightness is greater the closer the star is to us.

onde $\sigma$ (letra grega sigma) é uma constante, como o $\pi$ (pi). problems.problem:
Kepler's Laws describe the motions of planets, moons, comets and artificial satellites around the bodies they orbit. They hold for the Sun and its planets and for the planets and their natural or artificial satellites.

Kepler's 1st Law states that:

"The planets (including dwarf planets) revolve around the Sun in elliptical orbits, with the Sun at one of the foci of the ellipse."

Kepler's 2nd Law states that:

"In equal intervals of time ($\Delta t_{12} = \Delta t_{34}$) the planets "sweep" equal areas ($\text{Area}_1 = \text{Area}_2$)."

Kepler's 3rd Law states that $T^2 = k a^3$, where $k = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{G\,(M_{Sun} + M_{Planet})}$, $G$ is the Universal Gravitation constant and $a$ is the semi-major axis of the ellipse.

As a consequence of the three Kepler's Laws we can state that:

Attention: FIRST write F (false) or T (true) in front of each statement and THEN choose the option that contains the correct sequence of F and T.

1st) At perihelion the speed of the planets is greater than at aphelion. See figure.
2nd) Since the mass of the planets is negligible compared with the mass of the Sun, the value of the constant $k$ is practically the same for all bodies of the Solar System that orbit the Sun.
3rd) At points $P_1$ and $P_4$ the speeds of the planets are increasing, but decreasing at points $P_2$ and $P_3$. Consider that the body will pass through points $P_1$, $P_2$, $P_3$, $P_4$ in this order.
4th) The greater the semi-major axis of the planet's ellipse, the longer its year.
5th) Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation invalidated the three Kepler's Laws.

Mark the option that contains the correct sequence of F and T.
a) 1st (T) - 2nd (T) - 3rd (F) - 4th (T) - 5th (F).
b) 1st (T) - 2nd (T) - 3rd (T) - 4th (T) - 5th (F).
c) 1st (F) - 2nd (F) - 3rd (T) - 4th (T) - 5th (F).
d) 1st (F) - 2nd (F) - 3rd (F) - 4th (F) - 5th (T).
e) 1st (T) - 2nd (T) - 3rd (F) - 4th (F) - 5th (T).

problems.problem:
Kepler's Laws describe the motions of planets, moons, comets and artificial satellites around the bodies they orbit. They hold for the Sun and its planets and for the planets and their natural or artificial satellites.

Kepler's 1st Law states that:

"The planets (including dwarf planets) revolve around the Sun in elliptical orbits, with the Sun at one of the foci of the ellipse."

Kepler's 2nd Law states that:

"In equal intervals of time ($\Delta t_{12} = \Delta t_{34}$) the planets "sweep" equal areas ($\text{Area}_1 = \text{Area}_2$)."

Kepler's 3rd Law states that $T^2 = k a^3$, where $T$ is the orbital period, $a$ is the semi-major axis of the ellipse, $k = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{G\,(M_{Sun} + M_{Planet})}$, and $G$ is the Universal Gravitation constant.

3rd) In equal intervals of time the planets "sweep" equal areas.
4th) The gravitational force between the Sun and the body is maximum while it is near the centre of the arc $P_1P_2$.
5th) The Sun is always at the centre of the ellipse, that is, of the orbit of the body.

Mark the option that contains the correct sequence of F and T.

problems.problem:
Rockets rise because they throw gases at high speed downwards, generating an upward force (called thrust) that overcomes the rocket's weight. This force depends on two main factors: 1) the amount of mass of propellant "burned" per second and 2) the speed with which the gases are ejected by the rocket engine.

That is, the more propellant the rocket "burns" per second and the faster the gases are ejected, the greater the thrust that pushes the rocket upwards.

Based on this information, which of the rockets below will have the greatest thrust when launched?
a) A rocket that burns little propellant and throws the gases slowly.
b) A rocket that burns a lot of propellant, but the gases are thrown very slowly.
c) A rocket that burns little propellant, but throws the gases very fast.
d) A rocket that burns a lot of propellant and throws the gases with a lot of speed.
e) A rocket that does not burn propellant, but spins very fast.
problems.problem_orig:
Os foguetes sobem porque lançam gases em alta velocidade para baixo, gerando uma força para cima (chamada de força empuxo) que vence a força peso do foguete. Essa força depende de dois fatores principais: 1) da quantidade de massa de propelente "queimado" por segundo e 2) da velocidade com que os gases são ejetados pelo motor do foguete.

Ou seja, quanto mais propelente o foguete "queima" por segundo e mais rápido os gases são ejetados, maior será a força empuxo que empurra o foguete para cima.

Com base nestas informações, qual dos foguetes abaixo terá maior força de empuxo ao ser lançado?
a) Um foguete que queima pouco propelente e lança os gases devagar.
b) Um foguete que queima muito propelente, mas os gases são lançados bem devagar.
c) Um foguete que queima pouco propelente, mas lança os gases muito rápido.
d) Um foguete que queima muito propelente e lança os gases com muita velocidade.
e) Um foguete que não queima propelente, mas gira muito rápido.

b) Satellites in low orbit take 24 hours to go around the Earth, just like geostationary satellites.
c) The lower the satellite, the slower it moves around the Earth.

e) Satellites in low orbits complete one revolution around the Earth every 90 minutes and can make up to 16 revolutions per day.

It operates in geostationary orbit, at 35786 km altitude above the equator. In this position, the satellite rotates with the same speed as the Earth, remaining fixed over the same point of the planet. This type of orbit allows the SGDC to maintain continuous communication with ground antennas, covering up to one third of the planet's surface - ideal for connecting the entire Brazilian territory with a single satellite.

b) Satellites such as the SGDC are used only for scientific purposes, and not for communication or digital inclusion.

problems.problem:
PET-bottle rockets, with water and compressed air, move when the compressed air inside the bottle expels the water contained in the bottle, that is, it ejects the water (and air) at high speed and moves in the opposite direction.

PET-bottle rockets, with vinegar and baking soda, move when the gas generated by the chemical reaction between these two substances expels this liquid mixture at high speed and the rocket moves in the opposite direction.

Solid-propulsion rockets move when the gases from the burning of the propellant are ejected backwards at high speed and the rocket moves in the opposite direction.

That is, when something is ejected backwards, at high speed, the rocket moves in the opposite direction.

Mark the Law of Physics that explains the motion of the rockets described above.
a) The Law of Action and Reaction, by Sir Isaac Newton.
b) The Law of Inertia, by Sir Isaac Newton.
c) The Fundamental Law of Mechanics which says that force is equal to acceleration.
d) The First Law of Thermodynamics.
e) The Theory of General Relativity, by Albert Einstein.
problems.problem_orig:
Os foguetes de garrafas PET, com água e ar comprimido, se movem quando o ar comprimido dentro da garrafa expulsa a água contida dentro da garrafa, ou seja, ejeta a água (e ar) em alta velocidade e se move na direção oposta.

Os foguetes de garrafas PET, com vinagre e bicarbonato de sódio, se movem quando o gás gerado pela reação química entre estas duas substâncias expulsa esta mistura líquida em alta velocidade e o foguete se move na direção oposta.

Os foguetes de propulsão sólida se movem quando os gases da queima do propelente são ejetados para trás em alta velocidade e o foguete se move na direção oposta.

Ou seja, quando algo é ejetado para trás, em alta velocidade, o foguete se move no sentido oposto.

Assinale a Lei da Física que explica o movimento dos foguetes acima descritos.
a) A Lei da Ação-Reação, de Sir Isaac Newton.
b) A Lei da Inércia, de Sir Isaac Newton.
c) A Lei Fundamental da Mecânica que diz que força é igual a aceleração.
d) A Primeira Lei da Termodinâmica.
e) A Teoria da Relatividade Geral, de Albert Einstein.

problems.problem:
The Centenary Mission. On 30 March 2006, Brazil joined the select group of nations that have sent citizens into space. The astronaut Marcos Pontes lifted off from the Baikonur Cosmodrome, in Kazakhstan, aboard the Russian spacecraft Soyuz TMA-8. The mission was given this name, Centenary Mission, to celebrate the 100 years of Santos Dumont's flight in the 14-Bis. Pontes spent about 10 days on the International Space Station (ISS) carrying out scientific experiments.

The Centenary Mission, carried out in 2006, was a milestone for Brazilian space exploration. About this mission and the journey of the astronaut Marcos Pontes, mark the correct option:
a) The astronaut Marcos Pontes lifted off from a launch base located in Brazil, at the Alcantara Launch Centre (Maranhão).
b) The return of the Soyuz capsule, bringing the astronaut back to the Earth, took place through a soft landing in the Atlantic Ocean, near the Brazilian coast.
c) The spacecraft used to transport the astronaut was the Soyuz TMA-8, of Russian manufacture, departing from the Baikonur Cosmodrome.
d) The main objective of the mission was to take the first Brazilian meteorological satellite to be placed in orbit by Marcos Pontes personally.
e) Marcos Pontes remained in space for a year, carrying out external maintenance on the solar panels of the Moon.
problems.problem_orig:
A Missão Centenário. Em 30 de março de 2006, o Brasil entrou para o seleto grupo de nações que enviaram cidadãos ao espaço. O astronauta Marcos Pontes decolou do Cosmódromo de Baikonur, no Cazaquistão, a bordo da nave russa Soyuz TMA-8. A missão recebeu esse nome, Missão Centenário, para celebrar os 100 anos do voo de Santos Dumont no 14-Bis. Pontes passou cerca de 10 dias na Estação Espacial Internacional (ISS) realizando experimentos científicos.

A Missão Centenário, realizada em 2006, foi um marco para a exploração espacial brasileira. Sobre essa missão e a jornada do astronauta Marcos Pontes, assinale a alternativa correta:
a) O astronauta Marcos Pontes decolou de uma base de lançamentos localizada no Brasil, no Centro de Lançamento de Alcântara (Maranhão).
b) O retorno da cápsula Soyuz, trazendo o astronauta de volta à Terra, ocorreu através de um pouso suave no Oceano Atlântico, próximo à costa brasileira.
c) A nave utilizada para o transporte do astronauta foi a Soyuz TMA-8, de fabricação russa, partindo do Cosmódromo de Baikonur.
d) O objetivo principal da missão foi levar o primeiro satélite meteorológico brasileiro para ser colocado em órbita por Marcos Pontes pessoalmente.
e) Marcos Pontes permaneceu no espaço um ano, realizando manutenções externas nos painéis solares da Lua.

problems.problem:
Brazil has a series of satellites developed by INPE (National Institute for Space Research). This equipment is fundamental for the economy and for environmental preservation, since it makes it possible to monitor deforestation in the Amazon, monitor fires, plan the planting of agricultural crops and observe the level of rivers and water reservoirs etc.

The satellites of the CBERS family (China-Brazil Earth Resources Satellite) and the AMAZONIA-1 satellite are examples of cutting-edge technology developed by Brazil.

About the main use of these satellites, mark the correct option:
a) They are military defence satellites equipped with weapon systems to protect the Brazilian borders from space invasions.
b) They are remote sensing satellites, used mainly for monitoring deforestation, agriculture and environmental disasters.
c) They are communications satellites designed exclusively to transmit radio and television signals to the countries of Europe and Asia.
d) They are crewed satellites that serve as space stations so that Brazilian scientists can live and grow food in space for long periods.
e) They are navigation satellites that work like GPS, serving only to guide cargo ships crossing the Antarctic Ocean.
problems.problem_orig:
O Brasil possui uma série de satélites desenvolvidos pelo INPE (Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais). Esses equipamentos são fundamentais para a economia e para a preservação ambiental, pois permitem vigiar o desmatamento na Amazônia, monitorar queimadas, planejar o plantio de safras agrícolas e observar o nível dos rios e reservatórios de água etc.

Os satélites das famílias CBERS (Satélite Sino-Brasileiro de Recursos Terrestres) e o satélite AMAZONIA-1 são exemplos de tecnologia de ponta desenvolvida pelo Brasil.

Sobre a principal utilidade desses satélites, assinale a alternativa correta:
a) São satélites de defesa militar equipados com sistemas de armas para proteger as fronteiras brasileiras de invasões espaciais.
b) São satélites de sensoriamento remoto, utilizados principalmente para o monitoramento do desmatamento, da agricultura e de desastres ambientais.
c) São satélites de comunicações projetados exclusivamente para transmitir sinais de rádio e televisão para os países da Europa e Ásia.
d) São satélites tripulados que servem como estações espaciais para que cientistas brasileiros vivam e cultivem alimentos no espaço por longos períodos.
e) São satélites de navegação que funcionam como o GPS, servindo apenas para guiar navios de carga que cruzam o Oceano Antártico.
